class.name: UZUMapImport
class.brief_description: Brings normal and depth maps made outside the engine into line with a picture.
class.description: Normal and depth maps estimated by outside models or tools (no model ships with the engine) often come at another size, a few pixels off, in the DirectX normal convention, with denormalized vectors, with white meaning far, or with a narrow range. [UZUMapImport] checks and fixes each of these against the picture they belong to and reports what it found and what it changed, so an agent can trust or override it. - Size: resized to the picture (a different aspect ratio is reported as a warning). - Offset: the cross-correlation of the edges of the picture and of the map. The [code]found.offset_px[/code] value is where the picture's content sits in the map (map pixel = picture pixel + offset); the map is moved back when the match is clearly better. - Normal convention: judged from the picture's own shading; DirectX maps get their green flipped to OpenGL, which Godot expects. When the shading does not tell, the map is kept as is with a warning. Vectors are normalized. - Depth: white = near or far is judged from the bottom vs the top of the picture (or given with [enum DepthKind]); the result is a disparity map (white = near) stretched to 0..1. [b]Note:[/b] This class is specific to U.ZU Engine (U.ZU Picture).

method.name: import_file
method.description: Like [method import_map] with files: loads the map and the picture, saves the fixed map as a PNG to [param out_path]. Returns the same [Dictionary] with [code]"out"[/code] in place of [code]"image"[/code].

method.name: import_map
method.description: Returns [code]{"ok", "kind", "image", "found", "changed", "warnings"}[/code]: the fixed map (RGB8 for normals, L8 for depth, at the picture's size), what was found ([code]convention[/code], [code]offset_px[/code], [code]white_is[/code], ...), what was changed and anything to check by eye. [param align] [code]false[/code] skips the offset search.

constants.constant: Judge from the picture whether white is near or far.
